 Toddler snack sold at Costco, Target, Walmart recalled over potentially deadly hazard 
 Some children who consumed the snack were hospitalized, the FDA said. 
 By Izzy Stroobandt • 
 Published 4 hours ago • 
 Updated 4 hours ago 
 BOOKMARKER 
 You’re watching the NBC 5 Chicago News streaming channel, which plays local Chicago news 24 hours a day, seven days a week. You can find the “NBC 5 Chicago News” streaming channel on your phone or computer, and on Peacock, Samsung, Roku, Xumo or on our app, so you can watch our local news on your schedule.
 A toddler snack sold by several major retailers was recalled because of a potentially deadly hazard, according to the Food and Drug Administration. 
 All flavors, quantities and varieties of Once Upon A Farm's Tractor Wheels Organic Toddler Soft Baked-Bars were recalled after the FDA received several reports of toddlers "suffering complete airway obstruction with the inability to breathe after consuming the product," an alert on the agency's website states.
 Stream NBC 5 for free, 24/7, wherever you are.

 "When chewed, the product reportedly forms a dry, sticky mass that standard choking interventions — including back blows and the Heimlich maneuver — may fail to dislodge," the recall alert states. "Some reported choking incidents have required emergency response intervention and hospital observation."
 The snack is sold nationwide at stores that include Costco, Target and Walmart, and online at retailers including Amazon. 
 The FDA advised anyone with the snack to "immediately" throw it away.
